tracesTo: UserFlow: Weekly Member Engagement, Feed Interaction, Pick'ems & History Browsing

stories.title: Display Multi-Line Chart for Rankings Progression
stories.goal: see a visual chart showing how all teams' rankings have changed over time
stories.benefit: I can quickly understand ranking trends and see which teams are rising or falling throughout the season
acceptanceCriteria: Chart displays one line per team showing rank position over published weeks
Y-axis shows rank positions (1 at top, N at bottom) with inverted scale
X-axis shows week labels for all weeks with published rankings in selected time window
Each line is visually distinct with team colors or differentiated styling
Chart updates automatically when season or time window selection changes
Chart handles gaps in data when rankings are skipped for certain weeks

stories.title: Anchor Team Lines Using Stable Fantasy User IDs
stories.goal: track the same team/owner across multiple seasons even if team names change
stories.benefit: I can see long-term trends for team managers rather than team entities that may get renamed
acceptanceCriteria: System uses fantasy user ID from external platform as stable identifier for team tracking
Team lines maintain continuity across seasons in dynasty leagues
If team name changes between seasons, line continues for same fantasy user ID
Hovering over line shows current team name and historical names if changed
System handles cases where fantasy user ID ownership changes (trade of team)
For redraft leagues, system anchors by team slot rather than user ID

stories.title: Display Team Logos and Colors on Chart
stories.goal: easily identify which line represents which team using familiar visual elements
stories.benefit: I can quickly find my team and rivals without reading labels, making the chart more intuitive
acceptanceCriteria: Each line uses team's primary color from league settings or sensible default
Team logo appears in chart legend next to team name
Team logo appears at line endpoints (first and last week) on the chart
On hover/tap, team logo and name appear in tooltip at cursor position
Colors are sufficiently distinct to differentiate all teams even with 12+ lines
System provides fallback colors if teams don't have custom colors defined

stories.title: Select Time Window for Rankings Display
stories.goal: choose which portion of the season or history to view on the chart
stories.benefit: I can focus on specific time periods without cluttering the chart with too much data
acceptanceCriteria: User can select from preset time windows: Current Season, Last 4 Weeks, Last 8 Weeks, Season to Date, All Time
Custom date range selector allows choosing specific start and end weeks
Time window selection filters chart data to only show selected period
X-axis adjusts to show appropriate week labels for selected time window
System defaults to 'Current Season' view on initial page load
Selected time window persists across page refreshes via URL parameters or local storage

stories.title: Interact with Chart Data Points
stories.goal: click or hover on specific data points to see detailed information
stories.benefit: I can explore specific weeks and understand exact rank changes and context
acceptanceCriteria: Hovering over a data point shows tooltip with team name, rank, and week label
Tooltip includes rank change from previous week (+2, -1, etc.)
Clicking on data point navigates to that week's full rankings table view
Tooltip shows commissioner commentary excerpt for that team in that week if available
Touch devices show tooltip on tap with dismiss button or tap-away behavior
Hovering over a line highlights that specific team's line for easier tracking

stories.title: Toggle Team Visibility on Chart
stories.goal: show or hide specific teams to reduce visual clutter and focus on teams of interest
stories.benefit: I can compare specific teams directly without distraction from other lines
acceptanceCriteria: Chart legend includes checkboxes or toggle buttons for each team
Clicking team name or checkbox in legend toggles that team's line visibility
User can select/deselect multiple teams simultaneously
System remembers visibility preferences during session or across time window changes
Chart automatically rescales if focusing on subset of teams improves readability
Option to 'Show All' or 'Hide All' teams with single action

stories.title: Highlight My Team on Chart
stories.goal: easily identify my own team's line among all teams
stories.benefit: I can quickly focus on my team's trajectory without searching through the legend
acceptanceCriteria: If user has claimed team, their team's line is visually emphasized (thicker, brighter, or pulsing)
User's team appears first in the legend and is checked by default
Option to 'Focus on My Team' dims all other teams while keeping user's team prominent
My team's line remains visible even when other teams are toggled off
System identifies user's team based on authenticated user's team claim
Works correctly for users who manage multiple teams in league

stories.title: Display Chart on Mobile Devices
stories.goal: view the rankings trajectory chart on my phone with usable interactions
stories.benefit: I can check rankings trends on the go without needing a desktop computer
acceptanceCriteria: Chart is responsive and adapts to mobile screen widths
Touch interactions work smoothly for tapping data points and toggling teams
Legend is scrollable or collapsible to save screen space on mobile
Chart is readable in both portrait and landscape orientations
Pinch-to-zoom allows closer inspection of crowded chart areas on mobile
Mobile view may use simplified visualization if full chart is too complex

stories.title: Handle Missing or Incomplete Rankings Data
stories.goal: understand how the chart displays weeks where rankings were not published
stories.benefit: I can interpret gaps in the chart correctly and understand when data is unavailable
acceptanceCriteria: Chart shows dashed or dotted line segments when rankings data is missing for intermediate weeks
Missing weeks are indicated on X-axis with visual distinction (grayed out label)
Tooltip on missing week segment explains that rankings were not published that week
Chart connects available data points with interpolation line when gaps exist
If no rankings data exists for time window, chart displays informative message
System handles partial season data gracefully for new leagues with limited history

stories.title: Compare Rankings Across Multiple Seasons
stories.goal: view rankings trajectory spanning multiple seasons to see long-term trends
stories.benefit: I can understand multi-year performance patterns and identify consistently strong or weak teams
acceptanceCriteria: Time window selector includes 'All Seasons' option for dynasty leagues
Chart X-axis displays season breaks or labels when showing multi-season data
Lines maintain continuity for same fantasy user ID across season boundaries
Chart visually indicates season transitions (vertical separator line, color shading)
System handles cases where team changes fantasy user ID ownership between seasons
Performance remains acceptable with large datasets spanning multiple years
